title: Raiders name Kirk Cousins starting QB for Week 1; Fernando Mendoza to serve as a backup
content:
HENDERSON, Nev. — Kirk Cousins will start at quarterback for the Las Vegas Raiders in their Week 1 matchup against the Miami Dolphins, coach Klint Kubiak announced Wednesday.

Cousins, 38, will start for his fourth franchise after staving off Fernando Mendoza, the No. 1 pick in this year’s NFL Draft. The four-time Pro Bowler signed with the Raiders as a free agent this offseason after spending the past two seasons with the Atlanta Falcons.

“He’s played really good football,” Kubiak said. “Kirk’s had a really good offseason, very good camp. He earned it.”

The decision was expected because Cousins has taken first-team snaps ahead of Mendoza throughout training camp. Cousins was used sparingly during preseason games. After Cousins went 5-for-6 with a touchdown pass in the preseason opener, Kubiak said that QB1 was Cousins’ “job to lose.” But Kubiak waited to announce his starter, remaining keen on fostering competition among the quarterbacks until the very end.

“I don’t want anyone to be comfortable in their job,” Kubiak said after the Raiders’ second preseason game. “It should always be that way from all positions. We’ll just keep going forward.”

Cousins had some of the best seasons of his career while working with Kubiak in Minnesota. He earned a Pro Bowl nod in 2019 with Kubiak as his quarterbacks coach, and another in 2021 with Kubiak as his offensive coordinator. Andrew Janocko, now the Raiders’ offensive coordinator, was Cousins’ quarterbacks coach under Kubiak during that 2021 season.

Cousins made it clear the coaching staff was a reason he came to Las Vegas when he signed in April, and he expressed excitement about reuniting with Kubiak and Janocko at the start of training camp.

“I think they are better coaches in the sense that they’ve learned so much over the last few years,” Cousins said. “That’s a big encouragement for me to know that I’m with coaches that I really feel good about. That’s a big part of having success in this league.”

Kubiak said he has seen Cousins get better in their reunion, pinpointing his leadership and command of the offense as qualities that have improved.

Cousins earning the starting job also aligns with the preferences of Kubiak and general manager John Spytek to play a veteran quarterback ahead of Mendoza at the start of the rookie’s career. Mendoza has impressed since joining the team, with Kubiak saying the Heisman Trophy winner and national champion has been “as advertised.” Kubiak said it was clear Mendoza has improved since arriving in the spring.

Kubiak said the Raiders will do their best to replicate meaningful snaps for Mendoza while he’s a backup.

“You can build in young-guy reps into your practices,” Kubiak said. “There are things you can do. It’s never as good as getting all the reps in practice, but you do the best you can with what you got.”

Kubiak did not disclose whether there are plans for Mendoza to play this season.

Mendoza will be the first rookie quarterback drafted with the No. 1 pick not to start Week 1 since Baker Mayfield in 2018; each of the past six quarterbacks taken with the top pick started the regular-season opener. Kubiak said there have been positive and negative examples of both playing and sitting quarterbacks to start their careers, but he said he believes the competition built between Mendoza and Cousins will help the rookie develop.

“(Competition) makes players so much better faster than coaching,” Kubiak said. “When they have a guy in front of them that they can look up to and they can see how something is done, it’s gonna accelerate their growth.”

One example of a quarterback who thrived after sitting early in his career is Tom Brady, the Raiders’ minority owner who was a New England Patriots backup behind Drew Bledsoe for his rookie season in 2000 before stepping in for an injured Bledsoe during his second year. Brady went on to win his first of seven Super Bowls that season.

When asked whether Brady had any influence in the decision, Kubiak said, “We lean on him for a lot of things.”

“Talk to him multiple times a week, and he’s been extremely helpful for roster building, for schematics, for team building,” Kubiak said. “You name it, he’s been helpful with it. More than helpful, an extremely impressive resource.”
